title: Aharoni-Berger strong conjecture for bipartite graphs
statement:
Let $M_1,\dots,M_n$ be matchings of size $n+1$ in a bipartite graph. A **rainbow matching** is a matching whose edges can be assigned distinct indices $i$ so that each edge belongs to $M_i$.

**Aharoni-Berger strong conjecture.** Every collection of $n$ matchings of size $n+1$ in a bipartite graph admits a rainbow matching of size $n$.

The extra edge in each matching permits a full rainbow matching and implies the preceding bipartite $n-1$ conjecture by adjoining a common dummy edge. The bound $n+1$ is best possible, while the conjecture remains open in the supplied text.
source_name: Candida Bowtell, Andrea Freschi, Gal Kronenberg and Jun Yan, “A note on improved bounds for hypergraph rainbow matching problems”, arXiv:2501.03216 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03216

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2025).
